description: A layer is a logical split of code inside one application, while a tier is a separate physical deployment unit, so a three-project solution deployed as one web app is N-layer but single-tier.
UI depends on a business logic layer that depends on a data access layer, which makes the business rules depend at compile time on persistence details.
A structure where the Application Core defines the interfaces it needs and Infrastructure implements them, so every compile-time dependency points toward the core.
A port is an interface owned by the core, such as `IProductRepository`, and an adapter is the infrastructure class that implements it with a concrete technology such as EF Core.
A `<ProjectReference>` in a `.csproj` that lets one project use another's public types; the compiler rejects any use of a project you do not reference and any reference cycle.
The single place, usually `Program.cs`, where interfaces are bound to implementations in the DI container.
The C# access modifier that makes a type visible only inside its own assembly, used to keep adapters such as repository implementations out of reach of other projects.
